eligibility_note: Panel of about 40 EMDEs with own FE and system-GMM estimation; exposure is mobile-money usage (text says digital financial inclusion 'driven by mobile communications and internet access'), so it is a narrow but acceptable mobile proxy; outcome is output volatility (3-yr rolling SD of GDP per capita growth), which is borderline under 'output/productivity' (volatility, not level or growth). No income-group comparison, but >=10 economies is met. Eligible with scope caveats on both exposure and outcome.

income_group_note: No income-group results; paper says only 'EMDEs' and gives no country list or income classification. Record's 'not reported' entries are correct.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree (serious): causal wording ('exacerbates', 'amplifies', 'impact') with only 1-year lags of controls (the MM variables are contemporaneous) and system-GMM without any reported AR/Hansen diagnostics.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree (moderate): mobile-money transactions/accounts are direct but narrow, mobile-money-specific measures (author concedes 'rather narrow definition of fintech').
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: too_harsh (moderate would fit): sample is chosen 'solely' on data availability and is small, but this is common for mobile-money data; the real weakness (country list not reported) is a transparency issue.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree (moderate): 3-year rolling SD of growth in a 9-year panel creates overlapping windows and serial correlation.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree (serious is defensible): post hoc median split ('we conjecture'), quadratic concentration term 'not shown', Table 1 columns numbered (1),(3),(4), unstable coefficients across columns (e.g. VIX 4.379/4.867 vs 0.401).
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree (moderate): quadratic concentration result is 'not shown but available on request' (footnote 3) and alternative MM measures are only asserted in footnote 2.
risk_of_bias.why: Serious overall is appropriate: causal language, no credible handling of reverse causation (volatile economies adopting mobile money), tiny samples (75-158 obs) and a flexible, post hoc sub-sample design.

problems: No fabrication in numbers. Unsupported statement in record: exposure 'well-known to be dominated by a few countries such as Kenya' is not in the paper text (external claim). Record's reading of p.1805 ('lag all covariates by 1 year to tackle joint endogeneity concerns') is right; lagged DV is only in GMM. Record's 'about 40' sample statement is as the paper states (abstract '40 EMDEs'; actual N countries 24-38).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree (serious): ICT is not instrumented, authors write 'causes' and 'we can state with a sufficient degree of certainty that these relations are causal' based only on country x year FE, while conceding endogeneity for the employment regressions.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree (moderate): EU KLEMS ICT capital services per hour is a sensible industry-level input measure but ICT data end in 2007 and R&D/offshoring proxies are weak or interpolated.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree (moderate): 18-19 high-income European economies, years 1996-2007 for ICT, three countries dropped from the counterfactual.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree (moderate): employment-share polarization from ISCO groups ranked by average wage; no wage data (stated on p.4).
risk_of_bias.specification: agree (moderate): many sub-samples and column variants, though the demanding industry x country and country x year FE headline is reasonable.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree (moderate): nulls are reported, but fn 25 decomposition is 'not reported here' and counterfactual drops countries.
risk_of_bias.why: Serious is justified by explicit causal claims resting only on fixed effects with no strategy for reverse causation; the rest is a reasonably careful descriptive-econometric panel.

problems: No invented numbers found. Minor: record says Table 1 note is the only place Norway appears (Table 7 note also lists it); record says the appendix tables were not available (B1-B5 are in the text); locator for the conclusion quote is p.25. eligibility_note: 40 Belt and Road economies, 2006-2021, own OLS/FMOLS/PCSE/DOLS/spatial estimation; exposure is a PCA digital economy index built mainly from ICT indicators (broadband, telephones, internet, cellphone, ICT trade) but also including medium/high-tech manufacturing value added and per-capita services value added; outcomes GTFP (productivity) and renewable energy (resource). Eligible, with the exposure-contamination caveat; income-group split present (Table 16).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree (serious): causal wording ('will cause a decline') with FE/FMOLS/PCSE and lags only, no instrument, and a DE index that overlaps with GDP per capita and services controls.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree (moderate): PCA composite mixes ICT with non-ICT structural items (manufacturing value added, services value added), weights not reported, rescaled 0-1.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree (moderate): 40 BRI countries selected by data availability, interpolation of missing data, 16 low-income observations.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree (moderate): DEA-based GTFP with a single undesirable output; Malmquist-Luenberger is a growth index (mean 1.118) yet the paper also reads it as a level, and the text calls it 'growth rate of GTFP'.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree (serious is defensible): mixed I(0)/I(1) variables (Table 7) while text says all are order-one, tiny within R2 (0.216 FMOLS, 0.006-0.027 SDM), wrong table cross-references (mediation 'Table 6', DOLS 'Table 15'), and sign flips across lags.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree (moderate): text says total spatial effect is negative while Table 14 total is +3.841; 'mediation' claimed though DE coefficient barely changes (-0.425 to -0.404).
risk_of_bias.why: Serious is appropriate: causal language with no credible strategy, a contaminated composite exposure, and multiple internally inconsistent statements.

problems: No invented numbers. Record's paraphrase of the 0.1 change reverses the paper's wording ('decrease ... decline'); paper's text itself is inconsistent with its Table 15 (region labels) and Table 14 (total effect sign). Record correctly flags these.

eligibility_note: 118 economies (38 advanced, 80 emerging/developing), 1997-2017, own FE estimation with informality x ICT interactions; ICT capital deepening and internet penetration are exposures (ICT also acts as moderator); outcome is aggregate labour productivity growth; explicit advanced vs emerging/developing comparison. All criteria met.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: too_harsh (moderate): growth-rate/first-difference models with country and year FE and controls, an explicit discussion of reverse causality (fn 9) and hedged conclusions ('some evidence', modest effect); no instrument, so exogeneity is not established.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree (moderate): ICT capital services use US hedonic deflators and steady-state initial stocks; internet use is mostly consumer use; informality proxies (modelled VA, agricultural share) are indirect.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree (moderate): 118 of 131 TED countries, 11 late starters, unbalanced panel, 13 dropped for missing data.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree (moderate): GDP per person engaged (not hours), partly imputed labour quality, uneven national accounts in developing countries.
risk_of_bias.specification: too_harsh (moderate): 4 informality proxies x 3 ICT moderators x 3 samples are all reported in full, and the author states the evidence is limited; remaining concern is p<.10 significance across many tests.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree (moderate): lagged-level results 'not reported' (fn 18) and conclusion foregrounds significant level interactions over null VA and negative advanced results.
risk_of_bias.why: Standard panel FE in first differences with reasonable controls and cautious claims fits moderate; serious would need stronger causal language than the paper uses.

problems: Numbers match tables except result 7. Possible mislabel in the paper that the record does not flag: the dummy ΔINF D is described as 1 for declines in informality yet its coefficients are negative (-4.8, -3.3, -5.3), the same sign as continuous ΔINF, suggesting the coding is reversed or the note is wrong; interpretation of the 'stronger moderation' robustness (Tables A1-A2, fn 20) is therefore uncertain. Record states exposure as 'ICT capital services per worker'; the level variable ln kIT is described as ICT capital stock per worker (Fig. 3, Eq. 2), so exposure definition is slightly mixed. Record says the author 'argues first differences mitigate reverse causality (fn 9)': correct.
